title: Global Error Handling
description: Implement global exception handling in ASP.NET Core Web API.

data.text: **Global exception handling** centralizes how unexpected failures are translated into HTTP responses. Instead of wrapping every controller action in try/catch, you let a single piece of middleware observe the entire request pipeline and produce a uniform error payload when something goes wrong.

terms.definition: A component that participates in the request pipeline. Middleware can short-circuit a request or pass it to the next component.
Built-in middleware that catches exceptions, logs them, and re-executes an alternative branch to produce a custom response.
A .NET 8+ interface for a single-purpose exception handler that can be chained with other handlers.
An HTTP feature exposed to the exception handler branch that exposes the original exception and request path.
The standard logging abstraction in ASP.NET Core. Use it to record structured details about unhandled exceptions.

data.text: Middleware components form a pipeline around your endpoints. When a downstream component throws, the exception bubbles up the stack until a component decides to handle it. UseExceptionHandler sits near the front of the pipeline and re-executes a small branch that builds the final response.

data.caption: Lifecycle of an unhandled exception under UseExceptionHandler.
data.definition:
flowchart TD
  A[Incoming Request] --> B[UseExceptionHandler]
  B --> C[Routing]
  C --> D[AuthN / AuthZ]
  D --> E[Endpoint]
  E -->|throws| F[Exception bubbles up]
  F --> B
  B --> G[Re-execute error branch]
  G --> H[ProblemDetails Response]
  B --> I[ILogger captures exception]

data.text: UseExceptionHandler() registers middleware that catches unhandled exceptions and re-executes a small inline branch to produce the response. Pair it with AddProblemDetails() to get RFC 7807 payloads for free.

data.content: A minimal handler that logs the exception and writes a ProblemDetails response with status 500.

data.title: Hide Detail in Production
data.text: Never leak raw exception messages, stack traces, or connection strings to clients in production. The example above conditionally includes the message only when the environment is Development.

.NET 8 introduced IExceptionHandler. Each implementation handles a single exception type or category and returns true when it has produced a response. Multiple handlers can be chained in order, and the first one to return true wins.

data.content: A handler that converts a domain NotFoundException into a 404 ProblemDetails response.

cards.title: Try/Catch in Each Action
cards.description: Wrap every controller method in try/catch.
pros: Easy to add contextual recovery logic
cons: Inconsistent error shapes across the API
Easy to forget on a new endpoint

cards.title: Centralized UseExceptionHandler
cards.description: One middleware component owns error responses.
pros: Easy to add logging and telemetry in one place
cons: Must remember to register new handlers

cards.title: Chained IExceptionHandler
pros: Each handler focuses on one exception family

data.title: Order Matters
data.text: Register handlers from most specific to most general. The framework calls them in the order they were added, and the first one to return true produces the response.

UseStatusCodePages() converts empty error responses (such as a 404 from the routing system) into a body. Combined with AddProblemDetails(), it ensures even unmapped routes return a ProblemDetails payload.

data.title: Handling Empty Status Codes
data.content: Turn empty 404 responses into structured ProblemDetails.

data.text: Exercise: Build a Resilient Error Pipeline

data.title: Compose Handlers for a Sample API
data.description: Wire up a complete exception handling pipeline with three custom handlers.
steps: Define a domain NotFoundException, ValidationException, and ConflictException.
Implement an IExceptionHandler for each that produces a ProblemDetails response.
Register all three handlers with AddExceptionHandler<T>() in Program.cs.
Call AddProblemDetails() and UseExceptionHandler() to enable the pipeline.
Throw each exception from a test endpoint and verify the resulting status codes and content types.
data.expectedOutcome: Every unhandled exception maps to a ProblemDetails response with the correct status code, content type, and correlation id.

items.text: AddProblemDetails() is registered in the service container
UseStatusCodePages() converts empty 404 responses to ProblemDetails
Handlers log the exception with structured data (path, trace id)
Production responses hide internal exception details
Each domain exception family has its own IExceptionHandler

data.title: Key Takeaways
points: UseExceptionHandler centralizes error responses and logging
Pair it with AddProblemDetails for RFC 7807 payloads
Never expose internal exception messages in production
Add a trace id to every error response for supportability
data.takeaway: Global error handling turns brittle controller logic into a predictable, observable API.
